::: {#thm-inner-product-sign}

#### The sign of the inner product

For nonzero $\vx, \vy \in \reals^p$ with [angle](#def-angle) $\angpar \in [0, \pi]$ between them,

$$\dprod{\vx}{\vy} = \norm{\vx}_2 \norm{\vy}_2 \cos\angpar,$$

so:

- $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} > 0$
  when the vectors point broadly in the same [direction](vector-calculus.qmd#def-direction) ($\angpar < \pi/2$).
- $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} = 0$
  exactly when the vectors are [orthogonal](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-orthogonal-vectors) ($\angpar = \pi/2$).
- $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} < 0$
  when the vectors point broadly in opposing directions ($\angpar > \pi/2$).

:::

::: proof
By the definition of the [angle](#def-angle),
$\cos\angpar$ is the [cosine similarity](#def-cosine-similarity) $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} / (\norm{\vx}_2 \norm{\vy}_2)$,
which gives the displayed equation.
Both vectors are nonzero, so their [norms](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-norm) are positive,
and $\dprod{\vx}{\vy}$ has the sign of $\cos\angpar$.
On $[0, \pi]$, the [cosine](algebra-trigonometry.qmd#def-cosine-sine) is positive for $\angpar < \pi/2$, zero at $\pi/2$ and negative for $\angpar > \pi/2$.
:::
